summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated: valid, no diagnostics) and the new harness assurance_generated_test.go; no source or evidence file was touched. This turn follows the registered question 486d1abb02d149b084c6a6800b992c97-question-1 on shapes reaching the leader's read-index producer, keeping it active while requesting one experiment through the real Step entry points. The harness runs five probes on freshly elected three-voter clusters: empty-Entries MsgReadIndex on the leader, one-entry MsgReadIndex on the leader (positive control), empty MsgProp on the leader (guarded contrast), and empty/one-entry MsgReadIndex on a follower (forwarding hop). Each probe recovers any panic in the harness only, reports the recovered value verbatim plus state, term, pending/queue sizes, committed index and emitted message types. Construction-time local runs (not the formal evidence) show the empty-Entries MsgReadIndex panicking inside the read-index producer with 'runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0', emitting no message and leaving the leader in StateLeader, while the one-entry control emits two heartbeats and creates one pending status, the empty MsgProp panics deliberately with '1 stepped empty MsgProp', and a follower forwards the empty-Entries MsgReadIndex unchanged to the leader, so the malformed shape is relayed onto the leader's path. Four comparisons encode the duty 'a peer-delivered message shape must not abort the node': leader empty-Entries must not panic (expected violated), leader one-entry (control), follower shapes (control), and the deliberate empty-MsgProp panic as the contrast. No interpretation is claimed yet, since the conclusion must cite the controller's retained execution receipt; reachability through an embedding transport is recorded as an explicit assumption rather than an observation.
